assumptions: The opportunity is assessed at the stated planning stage, treating absent commercial validation as uncertainty rather than automatic failure.
The family company will permit limited voluntary workflow observation, but no customer-data, intellectual-property, exclusivity, or distribution rights are assumed until signed.
The proposed product retains explicit human approval and does not warrant OSD acceptance or replace licensed professional judgment.
The initial beachhead is Polish renewable-installation SMEs with enough quote volume and workflow complexity to use the product repeatedly.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Permissioned analysis of at least 50 historical cases showing frequent, preventable and economically material errors; several independent installer interviews followed by paid pilots at or near target pricing; measured reduction in margin loss or handover delay; observed onboarding, support and rule-maintenance costs; renewal or continued-use evidence; and a repeatable acquisition test with documented CAC and conversion would support a materially higher score.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Placing a validation gate before quote approval and handover connects preventable margin errors and document omissions to a concrete payment event. The insight is plausible and testable, but official workflows are relatively streamlined and incumbent products already cover adjacent quoting, document, and checklist functions.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: A costly underquote or rejected pack could create meaningful pain and attractive payback, but neither the frequency nor preventability of these losses is evidenced. No independent interviews, paid pilots, purchases, or renewal behavior validate willingness to pay 900-1,800 PLN monthly.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid setup fees and recurring branch subscriptions could provide good cash conversion and software-like margins. However, CAC, churn, support effort, rule-maintenance cost, liability expense, contribution margin, and owner earnings remain assumptions, while the proposed subscription is roughly an order of magnitude above a lightweight quoting substitute.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish renewable installers with 5-50 staff form a coherent initial segment with identifiable workflows and buyers. The candidate does not establish the reachable customer count, prevalence of costly errors, or whether the segment can support 250 customers at the proposed pricing.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: The candidate could specialize in cross-OSD and equipment validation, but Reonic and ecoCRM already bundle substantial workflow coverage, while Hydo and SolarEdge constrain price. Incumbents with installed workflows appear well positioned to add equivalent checks.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven rules engine could extend from PV into batteries, heat pumps, additional OSDs, equipment compatibility, margin benchmarks, and adjacent European markets. Expansion depends on first proving that localized rule maintenance creates transferable value rather than multiplying operational complexity.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: A permissioned error taxonomy and maintained equipment-rule library could compound modestly with usage. At present neither asset exists, baseline rules and forms are public, workflow access is nonexclusive and revocable, and competitors could reproduce or bundle the functionality.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Auditable validation across margin, equipment, and handover could outperform spreadsheets on accuracy and convenience. The magnitude of that improvement is unmeasured, and the offer must justify a large premium over low-cost or free alternatives that already provide quotation and document capabilities.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Changing operator forms, varied equipment, and accessible AI automation make rules-based validation feasible and potentially useful now. The same technology lowers entry barriers, while assisted online notification and existing vertical software reduce evidence of a uniquely favorable timing window.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family company provides an unusually practical design-partner starting point compatible with the founder's preferences. Wholesaler, association, and targeted-email channels are only proposed: there is no signed access, audience evidence, response rate, conversion rate, or validated CAC.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A 25,000 PLN, part-time validation effort fits the founder's capital, technical skills, and family-industry access, and AI can accelerate an initial product. Sustained rule accuracy, GDPR contracting, human review, liability management, data permissions, and support across OSD and equipment variants remain material execution risks.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the product and commercial promise to a verified loss-prevention layer that integrates with incumbent quoting systems, then price it against measured savings with a paid pilot and performance-linked component instead of competing as another broad installer workflow suite.
main_structural_strength: The founder has low-cost, legally usable access to a relevant operating workflow and the technical fit to run a capital-efficient, measurable design-partner test alongside existing employment.
primary_score_limiter: The candidate has not established a sufficiently differentiated, high-value paid wedge against capable bundled incumbents and much cheaper substitutes, leaving willingness to pay, retention, and scalable economics highly uncertain.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Incumbents already offer quotations, document management, completeness checks and compliance-oriented workflows, while Hydo provides margin calculation and unlimited quotations for 89 PLN net monthly and SolarEdge bundles proposal functionality at no additional fee; this directly challenges both differentiation and the proposed 900-1,800 PLN monthly price.
